messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime change that prefers the FP8 path for mixed-precision Mistral variants, we see a small but consistent perf regression on customer workload A (p95 token latency +18%). Trying to gather quick facts before filing an incident.

Ramon Li: Oof. Do we have a repro harness or a recent profile? Which selector change exactly?

Maya Patel: The selector now chooses fp8 kernels whenever model has quant_profile.fp8_compatible = true and seq_len <= 1024. Config changed in runtime: 
```json
{"kernel_selector": "latency_first", "fp8_preference_threshold": 0.7}
```
We rolled to dedicated yesterday at 02:10 UTC. Regression shows up only when KV cache hit rate is high (~>60%).

Eli Novak: Can you paste p50/p95 numbers and throughput before/after? Also which exact Mistral build (vX.Y.Z)?

Maya Patel: Sure — workload A (mistral-7b-v1.2, batch size dynamic, avg seq 220):
- before (int8 fallback path): p50=38ms, p95=120ms, tps=220
- after (fp8-preferred): p50=35ms, p95=142ms, tps=210
So p50 slightly better, p95 worse. We suspect KV cache copy paths for fp8 introduce extra alignment work on tail requests causing stalls.

Tomas Eriksson: Interesting. On my microbench of llama-2-13b fp8 kernels I saw lower variance, not higher p95. Any difference in kv layout? Was the KV copy using 32-byte vs 64-byte alignment change in the FP8 implementation?

Maya Patel: Yes — fp8 kernel uses packed kv layout with 32-byte lanes and inserts a small reorder when sequence wraps. That reorder is cheap normally but seems to interact with batching heuristics (we changed batch aggregator to wait an extra 1ms to increase batch fill for fp8).

Ramon Li: So two knobs changed: kernel layout + batching wait. Could be queueing effect: for long-tail requests, extra reorder runs on hot path and gets serialized by the batch lock, bumping p95.

Eli Novak: Quick experiment idea: revert batching wait only (keep fp8 kernels) and run the same workload. If p95 drops, blame batching heuristic. If not, blame kv reorder.

Sara Gomez: I've kicked off two controlled runs on the dedicated cluster:
1) revert only batching wait -> job id run-2143
2) revert only fp8_preference (force int8) -> job id run-2144
Links: https://ci.internal/jobs/run-2143 , https://ci.internal/jobs/run-2144

ops-bot: Scheduled run-2143 and run-2144 on dedicated-42. ETA ~25m.

Maya Patel: Thanks Sara. Also logging note — add a lightweight marker in the runtime logs when kv-reorder happens: `KV_REORDER=true` so we can correlate. I suspect reorder_count spikes on tail requests.

Tomas Eriksson: I ran a microprobe that forces kv wrap and measured reorder latency: median 0.12ms, 99th 3.8ms when under 80% concurrency. Under bursty load it jumped to 18ms. That matches p95 increase magnitude.

Ramon Li: If reorder is the problem, we can try two mitigations: a) move reorder off the hot lock (thread-local buffer + async flush) or b) avoid choosing fp8 kernel when kv_hit_rate > 75% (policy-level short-circuit). Both are feasible but (a) is more work.

Eli Novak: I favor (b) as a quick mitigation (runtime policy) + async reorder as tech debt. Can we add a policy that says `prefer_fp8 && kv_hit_rate < 0.75`?

Maya Patel: Yes, we can compute kv_hit_rate in router and attach to request metadata. Quick patch looks like: `if(metadata.kv_hitrate >= 0.75) choose_kernel(int8)` in selector. I'll draft a canary.

Sara Gomez: Patch in PR #4221 with canary flag `fp8_kv_safety = true`. Deploying as a percent rollout to prod-dedicated 10% first.

Maya Patel: Also share profiling snippet for anyone wanting to reproduce locally:
```bash
# run harness with kv_hit toggles
./harness --model mistral-7b --seq 220 --kv_hit_rate 0.8 --selector fp8-pref --duration 10m --report perf.json
jq '.p95,.p50' perf.json
```

Eli Novak: Great. If the canary looks good, let's bake the selector change into the 1.2.1 runtime. Also add a regression test in perf-ci that runs heavy-kv scenario at low concurrency to catch p95 regressions.

Tomas Eriksson: FYI I ran the harness against qwen-14b variant and didn't see the reorder issue — qwen's kv layout differs (64-byte lanes). So this is model-specific; we'll need model profiles.

Maya Patel: Agreed — Mistral seems susceptible due to lane packing. I'll assemble a short model-profile doc listing preferred kernel for each model under different kv_hitrate ranges (llama-2: fp8-ok if kv_hitrate<0.9, mistral-7b: avoid fp8 if kv_hitrate>0.75, qwen-14b: fp8-ok across hits).

Sara Gomez: Noted. PR and canary links posted in #deploys. I'll keep monitoring. :eyes:

Ramon Li: Thanks everyone. Next steps: observe run-2143/2144, if run-2143 (batch revert) fixes, consider lowering batch wait permanently; if run-2144 fixes, apply kv_hitrate safety policy. Either way add perf-ci regression test.

Maya Patel: I'll file a follow-up RFC for async-kv-reorder (longer-term), and post the model-profile doc once draft is ready. Thanks! :rocket:
